Once a member of D.E.E.P., she was cast out and later joined the Pioneer squad.

lines.text: I am Nayuta, the fourth member of the Forerunners. I eagerly anticipate the privilege of working alongside thee.
Great Hero, thou standest within the very eye of the tempest. Take heed that thou lose not thy center, lest thou be swept away.
To think that fate hath brought us together. Truly, the threads of destiny are most enigmatic, are they not?
Haha. To think I should be so gladdened to stand by thy side. Truly, thou dost possess a talent both precious and perilous.
Perchance I must set forth upon a far voyage once again. Yet for the present, I shall steadfastly remain by thy side.
Thou, Great Hero, art now and forevermore the key of utmost import to all that must be done. Verily, 'tis prudent to care for thine own well-being.
I came to seek the Great Hero... Yet, it seems no soul is present. Pray, have I strayed upon a way most errant?
Haha. Thou art as busy as ever. I shall remain in quiet meditation. Return at thy leisure, when thy affairs be done.
Is this perchance the Great Hero's private paradise? Verily, a realm steeped in romance most profound.
This place is most wondrous, verily. Though vast it be, no matter the distance I traverse, my steps return me to where I began.
In every corner, affection for thee overfloweth, Great Hero. Thou art rich in virtue, and bear'st many a burden besides.

To be summoned to partake in the Great Hero's journey, 'tis an honor most profound.
I shall tread this path with an earnest heart,
that the journey be not in vain.
I thank thee most sincerely for bestowing such care upon me.
Haha. Ne'er have I known such hospitality as this.
Is this... the craft wrought by mankind's toil? Verily, I am filled with awe profound.
Oh, that even one such as I should be thus gifted...! Truly, thou art a soul of vast magnanimity.
To be thus honored by one so esteemed, I offer thee my deepest thanks.
Haha. So this is how the Great Hero doth win the favor of fair maidens. Verily, it doth stir the heart with delight.
Art thou acquainted with the power of bonds divine? Methinks I do now experience their very essence.
To think my bond with Great Hero hath grown so deep... I grow afeared of the parting that may come one day.
My trust in Great Hero hath surely grown profound. Pray tell, doth thy trust in me likewise deepen?
Since thou hast called upon me, I shall gladly accompany thee.
Didst thou summon me?
Hmm... is this not the path?
Ah, 'tis a meeting with the foe.
I know not if I shall prove of any aid.
Haha. Thy faith doth make me blush.
We face this foe with steadfast hearts.
After such fierce strife there must be rest.
Art thou holding fast, Great Hero?
Haste maketh folly of the task.
I stand prepared.
From torment freed I shall attain enlightenment.
A fair current seemeth to grace us.
Fare thee well.
Such sorrow it is.
I shall carry on.
Hm...
'Tis sore.
Alas...

Alas, it seemeth I can go no further.
I pray thee forgive me that I could be of no aid.
This place too hath been cleared. Now let us continue forth upon our journey.

To triumph, I shall do whatsoever must be done.
The burden of sin is one which I shall bear alone.

Dost mine present visage strike thee as peculiar?
Ha... even I find it so.

Within this vessel of mine, the voices of the multitude of mine own likeness do proclaim.
Their aspirations and aims must needs be fulfilled.
One day, Great Hero, may thou behold a realm replete with lofty edifices and innumerable chariots, a world vibrant with the melodies of human narratives.
Though sin be laid upon me by all, I shall yet endeavor to restore the world unto the tranquility it once knew.
The hopes, tears, ire, and remorse of the multitude of mine own souls flow through this vessel. Thus, failure is naught but forbidden.

Ah... It seemeth thou art much occupied once more this day.
'Tis no matter. I too must needs attend to mine own affairs.

Verily the Great Hero hath cause for his busyness.
I shall remain here, presiding over the multitude likenesses of mine own self.

This place doth bring to mind a time of yore, when peace did reign.
Indeed, 'tis a most wondrous place.
I pray that, one day, Great Hero, thy paradise may stretch forth unto this very surface.

Hark! Though I inhabit this body, this place remaineth most perplexing.
Though I walk and walk, still doth the way elude me.
Upon the Great Hero's arduous path, we shall accompany thee, that thou mayest attain all that thou dost desire.
I am ever grateful for your sincerity, Great Hero.
I feel greatly honored to be thus bestowed with the highest regard.
Thou hast toiled greatly to amass so many treasures.

How could I refuse such a gift so thoughtfully prepared?
With much thanks, I shall accept it.
Thy regard doth humble me.
Once more this day, I stand in awe of the depth of thy kindness.

Strange indeed are the threads of fate...
That which I once deemed but a fleeting breeze hath burgeoned into a raging tempest.

Great Hero, I long to behold thee for many a day.
To gaze upon thy visage would bestow unbounded joy.
That this sacred bond betwixt thee and me endure, the multitude of mine own likeness shall endeavor.
The multitude stand ready.
Speak thy will.
Art thou sure 'tis to that place I must go?
A new encounter draweth nigh.
'Tis now the turn of the multitude.
I know not if I can restrain my strength.
I will prevail, without fail.
A short reprieve before I journey forth.
How art thou? Canst thou endure?
Excess oft begets naught but harm.
Great Hero.
With all sins laid upon me, forward shall I press.
Now. With all my might, onward.
To the next we shall advance.
This tide doth run most agreeable.
I shall persist forthwith.
Ow!
'Tis painful.
'Tis ill.

Alas, I triumphed not...
Forgive me, Great Hero.
Hath this sufficed to aid thee in thy journey, Great Hero?
Thou art exceeding fortunate to have acquaintance with me, Great Hero.
They say the world is broad and the strong many, yet none have won my wonder.
Chargest thou me with arrogance? Is it arrogant to speak the truth such as it is?
If thou wilt, Great Hero, I shall hew down any foe thou desirest. By fair or foul means, I care not.
Thou art of a different sort from any I have beheld, Great Hero. I sense a special power from thee.
No ill shall befall thee while I stand by thy side. I swear it.
I do detest to spend the time here idly. Hie thee hither.
'Tis boldness, Great Hero, to keep me waiting. Were it not thee, I would have fain departed ere now.
Dwell there folk in such a place? How grievously uncomfortable it must be.
Verily, I shall have to mend this place with mine own technological prowess. Thou mayest rejoice at thy leisure.
'Tis a vasty place, yea much more than it doth seem. Though I walk and walk, I merely return to my place of origin.
Thy choice is well made. By thy good wit, thou hast recognized me, the wisest of all.
Oh, I knew not such technology existed.
Thou mayest spare thine hand, for already am I complete.
Didst thou behold my greatness?
I might easily procure such a one as this, were I so disposed, yet I shall take it to honor thy sincerity.
Haha, seekest thou to impress me? Thou art wise indeed, Great Hero.
This pleases me. Dost thou have more?
Prepare thyself for wonder, for I shall not disappoint.
It seems thou hast discerned my singularity.
Verily, thy labor will bring thee no regret. I shall see to it well.
I knew thou wouldst call me.
It seems thou hast need of me.
What? Not this way?
'Tis time to teach the foolish.
The wait for battle nigh sapped my life.
At last I may run riot.
Keep thy distance and look on, Great Hero.
Thou seemest comfortable.
Thou art well-posted to look on.
'Tis done with but a turn of the wrist.
Art thou ready to be astonished?
Only the strongest may live.
Behold my might!
That was nothing.
How trivial.
Is that all?
Argh!
Ugh!
Insolence!
Mark my words, this is not the end...!
'Twas a trivial battle unfit for my might. The end was written from the beginning.
